0581c028f8.headline: Rapha returns to the WorldTour with Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe
0581c028f8.full_caption:
Rapha is back in the WorldTour peloton.

The British brand has signed a multi-year agreement to supply racing kit to Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe, taking over from Specialized. It returns to the top level after sitting out this season, following the end of its EF Education deal in 2025.

The partnership is billed as joint product development rather than simple supply. Rapha's in-house team will work with the squad's Head of Engineering, Dan Bigham, with the aim of building the fastest race kit possible. The 2027 collection will be unveiled in December.

Rapha previously outfitted Team Sky, Canyon-SRAM and EF.

Can a kit built around engineering give the team an edge on the road?

c5159370bf.headline: Van Aert joins court case over illegal access to riders' data
c5159370bf.full_caption:
Wout van Aert and his wife have joined a Belgian data-protection case as civil parties.

According to Belga, a municipal employee in La Louvière accessed the personal data of 30 cyclists between January and September 2023. Those named include Van Aert, Remco Evenepoel, Mathieu van der Poel and Greg Van Avermaet. The prosecutor in Mons has requested 120 hours of community service. No verdict has been reported yet.

Van Aert and Sarah De Bie are seeking a symbolic €400 in damages, which would be donated to charity. Their lawyer stressed the need to protect their privacy and that of their children.

Should riders get more protection for their personal data?
